name: Reed v. Town of Gilbert
summary: The Supreme Court held that laws distinguishing speech based on its content are content-based regulations subject to strict scrutiny, even if the law does not explicitly target a particular viewpoint.
significance: Petitioners cite this case to argue that Washington's law is content-based on its face — it restricts speech based on the message the therapist communicates — and therefore must be subject to strict scrutiny regardless of the government's benign intent.
